findings.claim: The new memorycard reads reuse the Engram project check, which denies any mem_search or mem_context that has no explicit `project` argument. memorycard resolves the project from the working directory when `project` is omitted, so the default call in a workflow-bound repository is denied as 'names no project'. In the other direction, a call that passes the workflow's `project` but a `cwd` pointing at another repository is allowed, and the gate never reads `cwd`.
evidence: The diff adds `memorycardProjectReadTool` with `check: checkEngramProject`, and `engramProjectGate` denies when `read.Project == ""`.
The gate reads only `Project` and `AllProjects` from `QueryArguments`. The tests build their calls with `Named` and `Project` only, so none sets `cwd` or leaves the project out.

The workspace memory instructions say memorycard 'resolves the project from the working directory; pass `project` (or `cwd`) when you work outside it'. I did not read the memorycard tool schema, so I could not confirm that `cwd` overrides `project`.

findings.claim: Existing installs gain two entries (one PreToolUse, one PostToolUse) and the Codex matcher changes. Until the user reinstalls and re-trusts the Codex handlers, memorycard reads are neither gated nor recorded as evidence. `status` will report the projection family as drifted. This is a deliberate and documented consequence of the change, so it is lower risk than the gate bypass in the previous finding.
